$comment: Cross-stack geodesy known-answer contract — 02_TRD §2.6.4 / §2.15. Reference values derived from GeographicLib (Karney's algorithm). pyproj.Geod uses the SAME algorithm via PROJ, and geographiclib-geodesic (npm) is Karney's official JS port, so the Node and Python stacks must reproduce these within 0.1%. Coordinates are [longitude, latitude]. Do not edit a value without re-deriving it and citing the source.

geodesicInverse.name: equator_quarter
geodesicInverse.note: a*pi/2; the equator is a geodesic. a = 6378137 m (WGS84).

geodesicInverse.name: one_degree_latitude_from_equator
geodesicInverse.note: Meridian arc equator -> 1 deg N, WGS84.

polygonAreaGeodesic.name: one_by_one_degree_cell_at_equator
polygonAreaGeodesic.note: ~12308.78 km^2. Matches 02_TRD §2.6.4 'area of a 1x1 deg cell at the equator ~ 12,308 km^2'.
